newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares end on high as Wall St soars again.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares end on high as Wall St soars again.

text.p: Dutch shares closed at a record high on Friday, the seventh in the last 10 trading sessions, boosted by a surge on Wall Street following U.S. Producer Price data which pointed to tame inflation.
The news sent Wall Street powering ahead, taking the AEX index up with it, dealers said. "Today's figures are pretty good, people feel good about inflation," said one dealer.

The AEX closed 6.73 points or 0.80 percent higher at a closing high 846.09, down from an all-time high of 848.48 reached at the outset as the market responded to Thursday's 136 point Dow gain on better than expected U.S. retail sales.

Prices in Amsterdam sagged around the midsession as some investors took profits and settled down to wait for developments on EMU from the weekend's informal meeting of EU finance ministers and next week's EU summit in Amsterdam.

Dealers said they were encouraged by news German finance minister Theo Waigel was "cautiously optimistic" agreement on the stability pact, aimed at maintaining budgetary restraint after EMU in 1999, could be reached in Amsterdam.
The market was given a second shot in the arm by the 0.3 percent U.S. May Producer Price Index fall which one analyst said showed the U.S. manufacturing sector was free of inflation.
Dealers said the gain on Wall Street -- 67 points by the time the Amsterdam market had closed at 1430 GMT -- boded well for another AEX rise on Monday.
"Wall Street is up again. That market will go up another 100 points today and that means we're up on Monday," said a dealer.
Many market watchers say brimming institutional coffers have been behind the AEX rally which has seen the index storm up from around 648 at the end of 1996.

"The institutions have got the money and it's got to go somewhere," said a dealer. "A lot of the institutions, and private investors, are scared that they'll miss the boat. This index is going higher," he said.
